Use the portrait's visible dark round-oval eyes, fine eyebrows, softly tapered face, small nose and gently full lips as face guidance. The hair is newly designed for this photograph. Her hair is clearly visible in the same frame. Her straight near-black hair has a deliberately disconnected two-tier cut. A short, dense, blunt micro-fringe forms a continuous horizontal edge across the upper forehead, leaving a clear band of forehead above both eyebrows. The smooth upper bob shell curves around the head and ends in a crisp blunt edge at the jaw on both sides. Two loose lower panels emerge naturally from beneath that short shell and fall well below the clavicles, ending together on the upper chest. The jaw-level edge sits visibly above those long lower panels with a large, abrupt difference in length; the lower panels stay loose and straight over the front of her ochre apron. Each tier belongs visibly to the same head, and the fringe, both upper edges and both lower endpoints can be read at once. Her left fingertips steady a transparent navigation slide flat in a waist-height manual projector tray while her right fingertips align its repaired edge with the guide. A narrow patch across the torn slide glows on the pale wall as part of the projected harbor-buoy image; a damp cloth and the salt-streaked porthole make the delayed voyage and delicate repair palpable. She has just lifted her face from the guide toward the photographer, head turned only slightly, shoulders easy, lips softly relaxed, the interruption held in a quiet, approachable look. Her black square-neck work top and worn ochre bib apron give the dark lower hair panels a clean contrasting surface. Make a vertical, near-front three-quarter waist-up photograph from face height, with the complete crown, forehead, both jaw edges, clavicles and long hair endpoints inside the frame. Her hands and the projector tray remain below the hair tips in the lower part of the picture. Soft porthole light and restrained fill keep every cut edge and fine strand readable; the warm projector lamp is a small supporting glow. Use natural perspective and enough depth of field for the whole hair structure, face and repairing fingers, with gentle separation from the cramped room. Preserve tangible skin and hair texture, calm sheltered hair and the intimate scale of a real occupied work moment.
